about.title: Citrus Heights Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Most people in Citrus Heights see their doctors close to home, at offices and urgent care clinics along Greenback Lane, Sunrise Boulevard, and Auburn Boulevard, then travel elsewhere in Sacramento County when a hospital stay is needed. That patchwork of providers is normal in a city of roughly 87,000, but it can make it hard to know who is responsible when something is missed, delayed, or done incorrectly. Medical malpractice in California is not simply a poor result. It means a physician, nurse, pharmacist, or facility did something a reasonably careful provider would not have done, and that departure caused harm. Proving that almost always requires a qualified medical expert to review the records and explain where care went off track. The state's MICRA rules also add a 90-day pre-suit notice, firm filing deadlines, and a cap on non-economic damages that adjusts upward each year. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect Citrus Heights residents with an independent attorney who can evaluate whether a claim is worth pursuing.

whyChoose.title: Why Citrus Heights Patients Use LawProactive

items.title: The clock runs differently for malpractice
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from the date you discovered the injury, and no more than three years from when it happened, to file. Getting connected early leaves room for the mandatory 90-day notice to the provider before suit.

items.title: An expert opinion is usually required
items.desc: A malpractice case in Citrus Heights nearly always needs a qualified medical expert to confirm the standard of care was breached. The attorneys in our network know how to obtain records and line up that review.

items.title: Free to connect, contingency to hire
items.desc: LawProactive costs nothing and does not represent you. The independent attorney you are matched with works on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery, and they can explain how the yearly-rising MICRA cap on non-economic damages may apply to your situation.

items.question: My doctor is in Citrus Heights but I was treated at a hospital elsewhere in Sacramento County. Where would a claim be handled?
items.answer: Medical malpractice claims are usually filed in the county where the negligent care took place, and for Citrus Heights residents that is generally Sacramento County even when the clinic and hospital are in different parts of it. Sometimes more than one provider shares responsibility, such as a local office that missed a result and a hospital that failed to follow up. An attorney can sort out who should receive the required 90-day notice and where the case belongs.

items.question: My surgery did not turn out the way I hoped. Is that malpractice?
items.answer: Not by itself. California law recognizes that medicine carries risk, and a bad outcome is only malpractice if the provider's care fell below what a reasonably careful professional would have done in the same circumstances. That is why a qualified medical expert is nearly always needed to review the records. An independent attorney can tell you whether your situation appears to meet that test before anyone commits to a case.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover in a California malpractice case?
items.answer: MICRA places a cap on non-economic damages, meaning things like pain and emotional distress, and that cap rises each year under current law. Economic losses such as medical bills, lost income, and future care are handled separately. The attorney you are connected with can explain how these rules fit the facts of your Citrus Heights claim without promising any particular result.
